description:
Blind-spot `2026-05-05-010706` documented that
`WritePrimitivesBenchmark._execute_aggregate_state_op`
(`benchbox/core/write_primitives/benchmark.py`) is exercised today only
by the live-Spark CLI command `benchbox run --platform pyspark
--benchmark write_primitives --queries sketch_df_*`. Unit tests exist
for the catalog loader, the PySpark factories with a MagicMock spark
session, and the `DataFrameWriteOperationsManager` methods -- but
nothing for the dispatch fork itself: ops partitioning into
"aggregate-state vs SQL parity" branches, `_resolve_platform_name`,
`_extract_spark_session`, the per-op result envelope, SKIPPED-on-
unsupported-platform / SKIPPED-on-Spark-version paths, validation-bound
checks on `aggregate_value`, and state-dir cleanup between iterations.

Result: dispatch-only regressions stay green in unit tests and surface
only on the next ad-hoc CLI run.

Sweep verification (2026-05-05): zero hits for
`_execute_aggregate_state_op` in `tests/`.

anti_patterns.dont: leak the mock manager into integration tests
anti_patterns.why: it is a unit-level testing helper, not a substitute for the real manager in larger flows.

anti_patterns.dont: make the new tests depend on a real PySpark install
anti_patterns.why: the whole point is to exercise dispatch without spinning up a JVM. The mock manager is the seam.

deferrals.reason:
Stretch goal pending evidence the unit tests miss a real
regression. Decision criterion: if the first month after w2-w4
land surfaces a dispatch regression that the new unit tests did
not catch, file a follow-up TODO to run `benchbox run --platform
pyspark --queries sketch_df_*` against a real Spark in a nightly
job. Otherwise the unit-test coverage is sufficient.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Nightly live-Spark CI lane explicitly gated on a dispatch regression evading the new unit tests; no such regression evidenced.
deferrals.summary: Wire the live-Spark CLI command into a nightly CI lane

preserves.behavior: Existing unit tests in `test_pyspark_sketch_factories.py`, `test_dataframe_aggregate_state_ops.py`, `test_aggregate_state_catalog.py` remain unchanged.
MagicMock objects in existing tests are not promoted to the new mock manager helper (the existing tests have a different scope).
The live-Spark CLI command `benchbox run --platform pyspark --benchmark write_primitives --queries sketch_df_hll_persist_merge` continues to work end-to-end on a host with PySpark installed.

verifications.description: Dispatch test file has at least 6 passing tests
Existing fast unit tests still pass

work_units.notes:
Add `tests/unit/core/write_primitives/_mock_manager.py` that
returns configurable `DataFrameWriteResult` objects from
`execute_aggregate_persist` / `execute_aggregate_merge`. Allow
callers to inject success / error / metrics / aggregate_value.
Keep it MagicMock-light so it documents the contract.

Test `_execute_aggregate_state_op` with a mock manager that
returns a SUCCESS result whose `aggregate_value` is inside the
validation bound. Assert: result envelope has SUCCESS status, the
right metric fields, no spurious validation errors.
work_units.summary: Cover the success path: bound-passing aggregate_value

work_units.notes:
Three tests, one per failure mode. Persist FAIL: manager raises /
returns failure on `execute_aggregate_persist`. Merge FAIL: same
on `execute_aggregate_merge`. Bound violation: SUCCESS result
whose `aggregate_value` is outside the bound. Assert: each
produces a distinct, diagnostic error message in the result
envelope.
work_units.summary: Cover failure paths: persist failure, merge failure, bound violation

work_units.notes:
Test SKIPPED-on-unsupported-platform: dispatch sees a platform
that doesn't expose aggregate-state factories. Test SKIPPED-on-
Spark-version: dispatch sees Spark 3.4.x where `F.approx_top_k_*`
is missing. Assert: SKIPPED status with a reason string that names
the missing capability.
work_units.summary: Cover the SKIP paths: unsupported platform, Spark version guard
